B4 S5 (#385) — the standing instructions the player leaves for a DESK to carry out, and what the halt says when the desk cannot carry one out. #124's second must-handle class: a bite runs the store on your standing orders, so an order nobody can execute is the run proceeding on a policy that is not actually in force. That is a decision — put the dial back, or hire/grow the desk — and a decision is what stops a run.

An order only counts when the player has moved the dial OFF its default: the default IS 'no instruction' (market pricing is the honest suggestion the store already stamps, a flat lean expresses no preference, and the default posture makes no bet on the mix). A player who never touched a dial is never halted, which is what keeps this a consequence of a choice rather than a tax on the ladder.

Which desk executes which order lives in code (`src/app/deskOrders.ts`), against the SAME act-gate reads `buildManagerStatus` owns — the #371 lesson: a capability boolean that lives in two places is two places to disagree.
_ordersDoc: `subject` fills the `{subject}` slot of the `desk_order` halt in `data/clock-bites.json`, so the halt's cadence is written once there and who-could-not-do-what once here. Each sentence names the desk and the dial, because those are the two things the player can act on.

orders.subject: Nobody on your used desk can hold the pricing strategy you set
Nobody on your used desk can stock to the sourcing lean you set
You have no finance manager to hold the F&I posture you set
